ranking.decision: If export inputs are identical, investigate checkpoint selection and whether the loss reaches the exported encoder; if inputs differ but assignments do not, investigate quantizer sensitivity and assignment margins.

If gains are concentrated or neighbourhood/prefix metrics degrade, do not use ER alone to admit the code artifact; prioritize catalogue coverage and beam-search-consumed structure in the next objective.
If Stage-3 seed variability explains the observed differences, treat the current quality ordering as unresolved and base decisions on a matched-seed evaluation rather than single-run scores.
If treatment codes are less stable, require stability measurements alongside ER before advancing them to downstream evaluation.
If ER and Stage-3 candidate quality diverge in these paired measurements, retain ER only as an admission signal and add a downstream retrieval-quality criterion before accepting a mechanism.
